content: Proventil HFA, also known by its synonyms and brand names, is primarily used for the treatment of acute episodes of bronchospasm or for the prevention of asthmatic symptoms. The standard dosage for adults and children aged 4 years and older is two inhalations, which can be repeated every 4 to 6 hours. It is not recommended to administer the medication more frequently or to use a larger number of inhalations than prescribed. In some patients, a single inhalation every 4 hours may suffice. Each actuation of the Proventil HFA Inhalation Aerosol delivers 108 micrograms of albuterol sulfate, which is equivalent to 90 micrograms of albuterol base, from the mouthpiece. It is advised to prime the inhaler before its first use or if it has not been used for more than two weeks. This is done by releasing four test sprays into the air, away from the face. For detailed dosing instructions, refer to the FDA package insert, which also provides information on indications, contraindications, side effects, and drug interactions. Additional resources include online calculators for estimating creatinine clearance using various formulas and for converting patient weight from pounds to kilograms for accurate dosing. Recent publications, state-of-the-art reviews, textbook information, and trial resources are available for further reference. These include ongoing clinical trials, trial results, and evidence-based guidelines such as those from the U.S. National Guidelines Clearinghouse and the Cochrane Collaboration. Cost-effectiveness analyses of Proventil HFA are also accessible. Media resources, including PowerPoint slides, images, videos, podcasts, and MP3s related to Proventil HFA, are available for educational purposes. Patient resources include information from the National Library of Medicine, discussion groups, handouts, blogs, and news articles about Proventil HFA. Additionally, international resources, such as materials in Spanish, are provided. This information has been adapted from the FDA package insert.
